refuted.fact: F98: the customer identification programme NPRM is "a joint proposed rule by FinCEN with the OCC, the Federal Reserve Board, the FDIC and the NCUA", cited to https://www.federalregister.gov/api/v1/documents/2026-12460.json
refuted.why: I fetched that exact JSON (200). Its agencies array contains only "DEPARTMENT OF THE TREASURY" and "Financial Crimes Enforcement Network". The OCC, Board, FDIC and NCUA appear nowhere in the cited record, so the cited page does not support the co-issuer list. The substance is true, but only in a different document: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/text/2026/06/22/2026-12460.txt, whose AGENCY line reads "Financial Crimes Enforcement Network and Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, Treasury; Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System; Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation; National Credit Union Administration." Re-attach that url. That text also shows the rule carries several RINs (OCC uses RIN 1557-AF53, docket OCC-2026-0331), so "RIN 1506-AB74" is FinCEN's RIN, not the rule's.

refuted.fact: F76: PPSI beneficial-ownership verification procedures must contain "the same elements as 31 CFR 1022.220(a)(2) (the bank customer identification programme rule)"
refuted.why: The NPRM's own regulatory text at proposed 31 CFR 1010.230(b)(2) says the elements of Sec. 1020.220(a)(2), and repeats 1020.220 four times in that paragraph. 31 CFR part 1022 is the MSB part and contains no CIP rule at all; the bank CIP rule is 1020.220. The string "1022.220(a)(2)" occurs exactly once in the whole 712 KB document, in the preamble, and is a typo the researcher copied without noticing the rule text contradicts it. Printing 1022.220 would print a CFR citation that does not exist.

refuted.fact: F22: the PPSI definition's two branches cited as 31 CFR 1010.100(ttt)(1)(A) and (1)(B)
refuted.why: The proposed text reads "(ttt) ... (1)(i) A subsidiary of an insured depository institution ...; or (ii) A subsidiary of an insured credit union ...". Roman numerals, not capital letters. (a)/(b)/(c) lettering belongs to OFAC's parallel 502.304, a different provision with a different structure.

refuted.fact: F60: the verbatim_quote "A transaction is not conducted or attempted by, at, or through a permitted payment stablecoin issuer only because a transfer by third parties results in an interaction with a permitted payment stablecoin issuer's smart contract."
refuted.why: Proposed 31 CFR 1033.320(g) actually reads "A transaction, for purposes of Sec. 1033.320, is not conducted or attempted by, at, or through ...". The researcher deleted ", for purposes of Sec. 1033.320," from the middle of the sentence while presenting it as verbatim. The substance is right; the quotation is not, and a writer quoting it as given would misquote the rule.

unsupported.fact: F104: "about $52,453 per non-subsidiary PPSI" (and the paired $36,760 and $22,987)
unsupported.why: The document says "$52,453 per non-IDI subsidiary PPSI" - a PPSI that is not a subsidiary of an insured depository institution - paired with "$24,983 per insured depository institution (IDI)-subsidiary PPSI". "Non-subsidiary PPSI" is a different concept and would mistranslate. F104 also drops the sentence that follows: the average first-year cost to the small PPSIs is estimated to range between $261,011 and $436,762.

unsupported.fact: F96: OCC rule title given as "Implementing the GENIUS Act for the Issuance of Stablecoins by Entities Subject to OCC Jurisdiction"
unsupported.why: Footnote 11 gives the title as "Implementing the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act for the Issuance of Stablecoins by Entities Subject to the Jurisdiction of the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, 91 FR 10202 (Mar. 2, 2026)". Citation, date and page are right; the title is an abbreviation presented as the title. The other three citations (FDIC 90 FR 59409 Dec. 19 2025; NCUA 91 FR 6531 Feb. 12 2026; Treasury 91 FR 16844 Apr. 3 2026) match footnote 11 exactly.

unsupported.fact: F33: the second minimum AML/CFT element described as "an independent audit function to test the programme"
unsupported.why: That is the BSA statutory phrase the NPRM quotes from 31 U.S.C. 5318(h)(1)(B), not what the proposal requires. Proposed 1033.210(b)(2) reads "Establishes independent AML/CFT program testing to be conducted by permitted payment stablecoin issuer personnel or by an outside party", and the preamble expressly says PPSIs without auditors or internal audit departments may use internal staff. Writing it as a required audit function overstates the obligation.

unsupported.fact: F91: "502.401(b) an additional $100,000 for each day a PPSI knowingly participates in such a violation"
unsupported.why: Proposed 502.401(b) says "a PPSI who knowingly violates the requirement to maintain an effective SCP". "Knowingly participates" is the wording of 12 U.S.C. 5905(b)(5)(C), a different provision. Two texts conflated in one sentence.

unsupported.fact: F16: 12 U.S.C. 5905(b)(5)(B)-(C) described as applying to "a permitted payment stablecoin issuer"
unsupported.why: Both tiers read "a permitted payment stablecoin issuer or institution-affiliated party of such permitted payment stablecoin issuer". The fact also skips 5905(b)(5)(A), which sets the same $100,000-per-day penalty for issuing a USD-denominated payment stablecoin without approval under 12 U.S.C. 5902.

unsupported.fact: F61: "if no suspect has been identified, filing may be delayed a further 30 days to identify one"
unsupported.why: Proposed 1033.320(b)(3) adds an absolute cap the fact omits: "but in no case shall reporting be delayed more than 60 calendar days after the date of such initial detection." A writer working from F61 alone could describe an open-ended extension.

unsupported.fact: F84: OFAC internal-controls element listed as identify / block-or-reject / retain records
unsupported.why: Proposed 502.201(b)(3)(i) has four sub-elements: (A) identifies, (B) blocks or rejects, (C) "Provides reports to OFAC as required, including those described in Sec. 502.102(b) and part 501 of this chapter", and (D) retains records. The reporting limb is dropped. The fact sheet's own three-item summary is the likely origin, but the fact is cited to the FR text, which has four.

unsupported.fact: F78: "the first time that Federal law has explicitly mandated that a particular U.S. person have an effective sanctions compliance program", recorded with is_vendor_claim false
unsupported.why: This is Treasury's own characterisation of the novelty of its statute, not an independently established legal-historical fact, and nothing in the document substantiates it. Under the brief's rule it belongs as "the agencies say", like F30/F41/F53.

additional_findings: MATERIAL MISS - the full date chain is printed in the document and the researcher never records it. The signature block reads "Dated: April 8, 2026. Andrea M. Gacki, Director, Financial Crimes Enforcement Network. Dated: April 8, 2026. Bradley T. Smith, Director, Office of Foreign Assets Control." and the closing line reads "[FR Doc. 2026-06963 Filed 4-9-26; 8:45 am]". So: signed and announced 8 April, filed for public inspection 9 April at 8:45 am, published and comment clock starts 10 April. This also disposes of unverified_or_excluded item 7, which claims a public-inspection timestamp could not be established because the API url carries a cache buster - the filing stamp is in the document itself.

MATERIAL MISS - the one BSA provision expressly carved out. The preamble says twice that "FinCEN is not proposing to apply to PPSIs Sec. 1010.630, which prohibits correspondent accounts for foreign shell banks, or Sec. 1010.670, which relates to summons and subpoenas on foreign banks, as the statutory authority authorizing those provisions apply only to certain types of financial institutions", and repeats it in the cost analysis ("Thus, this provision is not relevant to the cost of the proposed rule"). F73 records only 1033.610 and 1033.620, and not_said never mentions the carve-out. Note the document then contradicts itself: the proposed regulatory text nevertheless includes Sec. 1033.630, "Prohibition on correspondent accounts for foreign shell banks ... refer to Sec. 1010.630 of this chapter." If the article touches subpart F, state the exclusion and do not assert the shell-bank prohibition applies to PPSIs.

GAP NOW CLOSED - the Executive Order number. The researcher put it in must_not_write because the NPRM says "Executive Order 14294" in the body and "E.O. 14292" in footnote 320. I resolved it first-party: the Federal Register API returns exactly one presidential document titled "Fighting Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations", executive_order_number 14294, citation 90 FR 20363, signed 2025-05-09, published 2025-05-14 (https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/05/14/2025-08681/fighting-overcriminalization-in-federal-regulations). The body text is right, footnote 320 is a typo, and the writer may now state E.O. 14294.

The FR API record the researcher cites as a source (https://www.federalregister.gov/api/v1/documents/2026-06963.json) carries more than F6 reports, and is itself a first-party Office of the Federal Register record: dockets[0].documents[0] gives comment_count 89, comment_start_date 2026-04-10, comment_end_date 2026-06-10, regulations_dot_gov_open_for_comment false, checked_regulationsdotgov_at 2026-06-19. Excluding the count is defensible (regulations.gov is 403 here and 10 June conflicts with the 9 June DATES line), but the record should say "the Federal Register record mirrors 89 comments and a 10 June regulations.gov end date" rather than "could not be verified". The safe article line stays: the comment period closed and is not open on the check date.

Two formulaic urls that could have been constructed rather than searched for, flagged per the brief even though both resolve to the claimed documents: the uscode.house.gov "granuleid:USC-prelim-title12-sectionNNNN" pattern and federalregister.gov's "/documents/full_text/text/YYYY/MM/DD/DOCNUM.txt" pattern. I fetched both and the content matches, so neither is a fabrication in effect. For the reader-facing sources list, prefer https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-04-10/pdf/2026-06963.pdf (200, 86 pages, page 1 = FR 18582, verified) over the .txt, as the researcher itself suggests.

Two further internal inconsistencies in the NPRM not to repeat verbatim: the PRA section calls OFAC's new part 502 the "Payment Stablecoin Effective Sanctions Compliance Program Regulations" while the part heading and preamble call it the "Permitted Payment Stablecoin Issuer Effective Sanctions Compliance Program Regulations" (F77 quotes the correct one); and the amendment instruction for 31 CFR 1010.100 adds eleven paragraphs, (nnn) through (xxx), of which (nnn) and (ooo) are [Reserved] for the separate AML/CFT programme rulemaking - the nine substantive additions in F27 are right, but a count taken off the rule text gives eleven.

Everything in the heavy numeric material holds exactly as recorded: 91 FR 18582, pages 18582-18667, 86 pages, Docket FINCEN-2026-0100, RIN 1506-AB73, comments by June 9 2026, effective_on null, final rules effective 12 months after issuance, $5,000 SAR threshold against the $2,000 MSB threshold at 31 CFR 1022.320(a)(2), $10,000 CTR threshold "during a single business day", $3,000 Recordkeeping Rule, $10,000 extensions of credit and cross-border transfers, $1 million private banking account at 1010.605(m), $10 billion State threshold, $100,000/day OFAC penalties, IEEPA $377,700, TWEA $111,308, UMRA $193 million, ~50 PPSIs at 60/40, up to 42, up to 19 of 50 small, $1,798,558 / $1,042,670 / $1,294,633 and the $6,456,379 three-year average, ~450 ANPRM comments, ~55,000 and ~8,400 SARs, ~5,800 / 3,000 / ~six OFAC reports, hotline 1-866-556-3974, the Feb. 13 2026 exceptive relief order, and all four prior GENIUS Act rulemaking citations. The 12 U.S.C. 5903(a)(5)(A)(i)-(vi), 5903(a)(5)(B), 5903(a)(6)(B), 5903(f) and 5905(b)(5) quotations match uscode.house.gov word for word, as does the Pub. L. 119-27 sec. 20 effective-date note (enacted July 18 2025; the earlier of 18 months, or 120 days after final regulations).

Nothing breaches crypto.md: no price, market capitalisation, volume, yield or fund-flow figure was recorded as a fact, the section XII market-size figures were deliberately excluded, and no issuer is named. The not_said list correctly captures that the document names no PPSI - I confirmed the sentence "it is not yet determined which specific stablecoins will be payment stablecoins and which specific issuers will be PPSIs" verbatim. Vendor-claim flagging is sound and in places over-cautious (F58 is mostly plain regulatory fact; only its rationale is an assertion).
